gap: No result ChatGPT got states the battery claims on one basis: divided by battery size, the makers' lights-off "up to" hours imply about 3 mA average draw for the NuPhy Air75 V3 and 5 mA for the Keychron K3 Ultra 8K, against 21 to 25 mA for the Keychron K3 Max and the Lofree Flow boards, and with the lights on only NuPhy (60 to 100 h) and Lofree (14 to 17 h on the Flow 2 84) publish a figure at all.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com (cited in chat 2), mechkeyfoundry.com and keeb-finder.com (cited in chat 2). mkbguide already prints the raw figures with their conditions (Air75 V3 4,000 mAh, 60-100 h lit, 1,200 h unlit "lab conditions"; K3 Ultra 8K 2,600 mAh, 550 h unlit; Flow 2 84 3,000 mAh, 120 h unlit, 17 h lit; Flow Lite84 2,000 mAh, 80 h unlit), and mechkeyfoundry repeats the NuPhy and Lofree ones. What they lack is the same-basis step: none divides capacity by hours, none says a lit figure exists for only two makers, and mechkeyfoundry says Keychron publishes no hours for the K3 Max while Keychron's own listing read today says "up to 73 hours". keeb-finder has mAh only. The RTINGS low-profile page (cited in both chats) and its Air75 V3 review returned only navigation to my reader, so I could not check whether RTINGS already has a measured battery or height figure. I also could not open NuPhy's own page (HTTP 429 on every try), so the NuPhy numbers are second-hand from mkbguide and mechkeyfoundry.
decides: It confirms the NuPhy Air75 V3 as the pick for anyone who types with the backlight on: 60-100 h lit against 14-17 h for the Lofree Flow 2 84, roughly 4 to 7 times longer between charges on the makers' own figures. It also shows that the Keychron K3 Ultra 8K's 550 h and the K3 Max's 73 h are not a 7.5x real-world gap that can be read off the box: the K3 Ultra figure is a backlight-off number, and the K3 Max listing text I read gives no condition. For our linkable rows it sets the honest segment: the Lofree boards win on typing feel and price through our link, not on battery; the Flow 2 84 is a charge-every-few-days board with the lights on.
